title: The monotone total positivity conjecture for the Eulerian matrix
statement:
Let $A(n,k)$ be the Eulerian number, and let $A=(A(n+1,k))_{n,k\in\mathbb{N}}$ be the Eulerian matrix. For $i,j,r\in\mathbb{N}$, take the submatrix whose rows are indexed by $i,i+1,\ldots,i+r$ and whose columns are indexed by $j,j+1,\ldots,j+r$.

**Monotone total positivity conjecture.** For all $i,j,r\in\mathbb{N}$, the determinant of this submatrix is a monotonically increasing function of $i\in\mathbb{N}$.

This is proposed as a stronger form of total positivity for the Eulerian matrix. The supplied text gives no resolution, so the assertion remains open.
source_name: Francesco Brenti, “Some open problems on Coxeter groups and unimodality”, arXiv:2410.09897 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09897

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).
